sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security in Mauritania: Executive Summary
sources.organization: United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA), United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS), and Climate Security Mechanism
sources.temporal_coverage: Study based on literature and country fieldwork in 2023; executive summary published 26 September 2024.
sources.methodology: UN review and 2023 field visit with community, UN and government interviews.
sources.limitations: Executive summary only; pathways remain plausible, geographically broad and unquantified.

sources.title: Analyse du paysage climatique pour les enfants en Mauritanie (Climate Landscape Analysis for Children)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate and child-vulnerability analysis; report carries UNICEF Mauritania copyright 2024 and includes historical 2022 flood impacts.
sources.methodology: UNICEF synthesis of documents, policies, risk maps and stakeholder/youth input.
sources.limitations: Child climate-risk scores are not FCV measures; conditions may have changed.

sources.title: Mauritania: Refugee Emergency Response (as of 30 June 2024)
sources.organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
sources.temporal_coverage: Refugee-response snapshot as of 30 June 2024; published 2 August 2024.
sources.methodology: Two-page UNHCR operational response update using registration, arrival-monitoring and needs information.
sources.limitations: Historical operational snapshot; service plans and outputs are not impact evaluations.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Mauritania
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: GIEWS reference date 9 September 2025; includes 2025 lean-season food-security estimates and rainy-season conditions through August.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS synthesis of crop, rainfall, food-security and Cadre Harmonisé analysis.
sources.limitations: Seasonal 2025 snapshot, not an update on current 2026 conditions.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, p. 1, opening paragraph and climate-peace pathways introduction.
claims.paraphrase: The study identifies poverty, food insecurity, gender inequality, limited services and youth employment as peacebuilding pressures.
claims.limitations: Executive summary presents pathways, not causal estimates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate and environmental stresses may compound these challenges and complicate efforts to sustain peace.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, p. 2, first two climate-peace pathways.
claims.paraphrase: Outside Mbera, the study reports host-refugee grazing competition and possible water-access discord across refugee arrival cohorts.
claims.limitations: Summary gives no incident-level locations or measures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The study lists resource tensions among possible climate-peace pathways.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, p. 2, farmer-herder and inter-herder pathway.
claims.paraphrase: The study links changing rainfall and altered traditional transhumance to farmer-herder and inter-herder conflict.
claims.limitations: The executive summary does not provide local incident evidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Rainfall shifts alter movement practices, which the study links to conflict.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, p. 2, final pathway on gender, youth and security risk.
claims.paraphrase: Women and youth face marginalization and security risks amid livelihood disruption and displacement.
claims.limitations: The summary does not quantify the change in security risk.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate-disrupted livelihoods and displacement may heighten these risks.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, p. 1, methodology and coping-capacity description.
claims.paraphrase: The study identifies communal committees and government disaster-risk-reduction and climate-policy efforts as existing coping capacities.

claims.locator: Printed p. 15 (PDF p. 14), executive-summary findings; pp. 29-30 (PDF pp. 28-29), child-risk maps.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF rates child climate exposure and vulnerability high or very high in 11 wilayas; six highest-risk are Hodh El Chargui, Gorgol, Hodh El Gharbi, Guidimakha, Tagant and Assaba; poorest, least-served children face greatest risks.
affected_groups: children with limited access to basic services
claims.limitations: Composite child climate-risk score; it is not an FCV classification.

claims.locator: Printed p. 34 (PDF p. 33), drought and water-scarcity trends.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF estimates about half of Hodh El Chargui communities face severe or high drought risk.
claims.limitations: The report does not name communities or provide a current update.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 35-36 (PDF pp. 34-35), effects of water scarcity and drought on children.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF links drought and water scarcity to rainfed-crop and livestock losses, child poverty and malnutrition, rural out-migration, and possible abuse or exploitation when families send children to cities.
claims.limitations: No local protection-incident rates are measured.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate-related livelihood loss and migration may increase child-protection exposure.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 38-39 (PDF pp. 37-38), 2022 flood impacts and child protection/service disruption.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports 2022 flood damage in Tagant, Assaba and Hodh El Gharbi; it warns flood displacement can expose children to violence, exploitation and trafficking.
claims.limitations: The report's house-loss totals differ; none is repeated here.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Flood displacement may heighten children's protection risks.

claims.locator: PDF p. 1, overall country situation and Mbera Camp figures; as-of date shown in report header.
claims.paraphrase: As of 30 June 2024, Mbera hosted 108,059 registered refugees; women and children were 83% of camp registrants.
claims.limitations: Historical registration snapshot; it should not be read as a 2026 population estimate.

claims.locator: PDF p. 1, overall situation; PDF p. 2, out-of-camp response and Population Flow Monitoring.
claims.paraphrase: UNHCR reports Mali's humanitarian-security crisis drove arrivals into Hodh Chargui, with camp saturation sending many to neighboring villages and straining services and natural resources in a poor, climate-shock-vulnerable region.
claims.limitations: Report links displacement to resource strain but does not assess resulting violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Conflict-driven arrivals strain resources and services in a region vulnerable to climate shocks.

claims.locator: PDF p. 2, out-of-camp response paragraphs and map showing host communes.
claims.paraphrase: UNHCR reports monthly arrival monitoring in over 60 villages and an area-based response with partners and local authorities for refugees and host communities.
claims.limitations: The report states response objectives and monitoring, not effectiveness.

claims.locator: Country brief, reference date 9 September 2025, rainfall and crop conditions paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: By end-August 2025, rainfall deficits persisted in Hodh Ech Chargui and Hodh El Gharbi; dry spells and floods caused localized crop losses.
claims.limitations: Seasonal report; local crop-loss locations are not specified.

claims.locator: Country brief, reference date 9 September 2025, Hodh Ech Chargui food-security section.
claims.paraphrase: For June-August 2025, FAO reports about 44,000 refugees in Hodh Ech Chargui faced acute food insecurity, including over 6,000 in Phase 4; 17% of resident Mauritanians needed aid.
claims.limitations: These are 2025 seasonal estimates, not current 2026 figures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO attributes added host food insecurity to refugee-driven resource and service pressure.

claims.locator: Country brief, reference date 9 September 2025, 2025 crop-support paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports government support for irrigation infrastructure and inputs; rainfed support includes dam and dike work, seeds and improved equipment access.
claims.limitations: FAO describes support measures but does not evaluate their effectiveness.

access_audit.locator: All 3 pages of the original UN executive summary; especially pp. 1-2 for methodology, pathways, and capacities.
access_audit.notes: Opened the complete executive summary PDF. Publication date cross-checked against the UN Climate Security Mechanism page; the underlying longer study was not inspected.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 80-page UNICEF report; printed pp. 15-16, 34-39 and 28-30 for child-risk mapping, drought, livelihoods, floods and protection.
access_audit.notes: Opened the original PDF and read cited passages directly. Report credits UNICEF Mauritania copyright 2024; 2022 flood-loss counts vary within the report and are not repeated here.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 2-page UNHCR response PDF; p. 1 for arrivals, camp population and climate vulnerability; p. 2 for out-of-camp monitoring and assistance.
access_audit.notes: Opened the original operational update. It states publication date 2 August 2024 and situation date 30 June 2024; claims remain historical.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full FAO GIEWS country page; reference date 9 September 2025, rainfall, food-security and crop-support sections.
access_audit.notes: Opened the official FAO page and read the relevant paragraphs directly; seasonal estimates describe 2025, not current conditions.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Direct official download returned a document-unavailable error page.
access_audit.notes: The May 2025 UNHCR environment and climate factsheet search listing was not used as evidence; no substantive claim relies on its indexed text.

search_audit.query: Mauritania 2025 2026 climate shocks flood drought subnational Hodh El Chargui Brakna Guidimakha primary report OCHA UN
search_audit.outcome: Opened the UNICEF climate landscape report, FAO GIEWS page and UNHCR response PDF; retained named wilayas and historical reporting periods.

search_audit.query: Mauritania climate conflict pastoral resources Hodh El Chargui refugees Mbera camp 2024 2025 report UNHCR climate adaptation
search_audit.outcome: The UN climate-peace executive summary directly identifies grazing, water, transhumance and gender/youth pathways; UNHCR and FAO report displacement-related resource/service strain.

search_audit.query: Mauritania refugee host communities climate shocks pasture water access conflict Mbera camp UNHCR World Bank report
search_audit.outcome: UNHCR and FAO describe Mali-crisis displacement into Hodh Chargui, pressure on services and resources, and acute food insecurity affecting both refugees and host residents; no violence outcome is inferred.

search_audit.query: Mauritania climate security pastoralism land water conflict resilience capacity local government communities UN report PDF
search_audit.outcome: The opened UN summary identifies communal committees and government DRR/policy efforts; UNHCR reports village arrival monitoring and area-based response; FAO documents 2025 farm-support measures. Effectiveness is not established.

gaps: No inspected source establishes climate as a cause of armed violence in Mauritania; DPPA presents plausible pathways, not causal estimates or incident-level mapping.
Only the 3-page DPPA executive summary was accessible, not the underlying longer study; its geographic detail and evidence limits should be retained.
The UNICEF report's risk scores concern children and climate exposure/vulnerability, not FCV; the report carries 2024 copyright and should not be read as a 2026 update.
UNHCR 2024 and FAO 2025 population and food-security figures are dated snapshots; this extraction does not verify 2026 values.
The official UNHCR May 2025 environment and climate factsheet download returned an error page and its indexed text was excluded from evidence.
